newsitem.title: USA: More corp debt supply seen after about $6.4 bln wk.
newsitem.headline: More corp debt supply seen after about $6.4 bln wk.

text.p: Despite the volume of new corporate debt supply this week, opportunistic issuers are getting set to launch a new round of issues next week, dealers said.
"Issues may be tapped out for this week but just brace yourself because names are starting to materialize for next week already," one syndicate source said.
U.S. corporations brought approximately $6.4 billion in new straight corporate debt to market this week, taking advantage of sharply lower U.S. Treasury yields to finance debt.
Issuers rushed to tap the market early this week, fearing that a surprise to the upside in Friday's U.S. employment report might make the market less favorable.
On Friday, the Labor Department reported a 210,000 increase in October nonfarm payrolls. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent for the month.

The data met Wall Street expectations and confirmed a third-quarter slowdown in the U.S. economy. U.S. Treasuries traded up, sending the yield on the 30-year bond down to 6.59 percent. By late Friday morning, the yield on the T-bond stood at 6.66 percent compared with 6.64 percent at Thursday's close.
